newsitem.title: USA: MBIA sees no losses from Jayhawk deal.
newsitem.headline: MBIA sees no losses from Jayhawk deal.

text.p: MBIA Inc said Friday it does not expect to incur any losses as a result of insuring two sub-prime auto loan receivable transactions issued by Jayhawk Acception Corp, which has said it intends to seek bankruptcy protection.
"We are monitoring the Jayhawk situation very carefully and do not expect to experience any losses on either transaction, said Richaed Weill, MBIA's president.
He said the MBIA-insured issues are substantially over-collateralized and the assets supporting the transactions are held in what he called a "bankruptcy remote special purpose corporation."
"MBIA is in contact with Jayhawk to ensure that effective servicing continues on these portfolios," he said.

MBIA said the first of the two transactions, the $41.8 million Jayhawk Funding Trust I Series 1996 A, issued March 15, 1996, has an outstanding note balance of $3.2 million and is collateralized by $27.3 million of receivables.

The second transaction, called Jayhawk Funding Trust I Series 19966 B, issued August 7, 1996 with $42.9 million of insured notes, has an outstanding balance of $24.3 million and is secured by $66.8 million of receivables, he said.
MBIA, through its subsidiary, MBIA Insurance Corp, insures municipal bonds and structured finance transactions.
